items.note: Context: the 8/24 GHL go live checkin confirmed the NextGen to GHL appointment sync is running on the separate DigitalOcean instance that keeps MedStation PHI isolated for HIPAA, pushing appointment status every 15 minutes, but raised two defects: rescheduled appointments leave duplicate records because the sync account appears to lack delete rights on the mirror, and the sync overwrites the contact source field, destroying Google, Meta and LSA attribution. Deliverable: verify the 15 minute sync end to end, obtain delete rights and confirm reschedules no longer duplicate, stop the source overwrite and tag synced contacts Next Gen Sync. Dependencies: DigitalOcean mirror stability and MedStation IT granting delete rights. Done: one appointment record per booking after a reschedule, and source preserved with the tag applied. Board audit 2026-08-25 across all four boards with subitems: NextGen Mirror (12484780084) is the mirror build and is already Done, Source Tracking (12484780178) is Done and owns tracking configuration rather than sync behaviour, and nothing on Ads, Video or Web + SEO touches appointment sync. No existing item covers this, so it drafts as a new subitem under GHL Setup (12665521507).

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. At the 24 August go live checkin the NextGen to GHL appointment sync was confirmed running on the separate DigitalOcean instance that keeps MedStation patient data isolated for HIPAA, pushing appointment status into GHL every 15 minutes. Final verification against live data is still outstanding, and this is the last piece of the Weston pilot that has not been signed off.
  • Defect one, duplicate appointments. Rescheduling in NextGen produces two appointment records in GHL instead of one. The working theory from the session is that the sync account has read and write rights on the mirror but no delete right, so the superseded appointment is never removed. The team has not yet ruled out genuine double bookings by patients, so this needs confirming with MedStation before any logic changes.
  • Defect two, source overwrite. The sync currently writes the contact source field on contacts it touches, which wipes the original Google Ads, Meta Ads or LSA attribution the moment a patient books. Every synced contact ends up looking like it came from NextGen.
  • Verify the appointment status sync end to end against live NextGen data and confirm each status change lands in GHL inside the 15 minute window.
  • Request and confirm delete permission for the sync account on the NextGen mirror, then reproduce a reschedule and a cancellation and confirm GHL holds exactly one current appointment record afterwards.
  • Modify the sync so it no longer writes contact source on an existing contact, and add the tag "Next Gen Sync" to every contact it touches so NextGen originated records stay identifiable without destroying campaign attribution.
  • Dependencies. Depends on the DigitalOcean mirror connection staying stable and on MedStation IT granting delete rights, which sits outside our control. Do not change the Source Tracking configuration itself, which was verified complete on 17 August. The fix belongs in the sync, not in the tracking setup.
  • done = a rescheduled or cancelled NextGen appointment leaves exactly one matching appointment record in GHL with no duplicate, and a contact that syncs from NextGen keeps its original source value and carries the "Next Gen Sync" tag.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

Deliverable: build a workflow that waits 30 minutes after the webhook fires then maps UTM and campaign values onto the contact the sync has created, matched on phone or email. payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. The 24 August go live checkin clarified how the booking flow actually behaves. The booking app webhook does carry the UTM and campaign parameters, but it does not create the appointment in GHL. The appointment arrives separately through the NextGen appointment sync, on its own schedule. That timing gap is the whole problem.
  • Why mapping at webhook time fails. If the webhook writes campaign data the moment it fires, the matching contact usually does not exist yet, so GHL creates a second contact. The booking then lands on one record and the attribution on another, and neither is complete.
  • Build a delayed workflow that waits 30 minutes after the webhook is received, then maps the UTM and campaign parameters onto the contact the NextGen sync has created by that point, matching on phone number first and email as a fallback. Do not let the workflow create a contact if no match is found; log the miss instead so the window can be tuned.
  • Chase the spec. The integration detail requested on 17 August has still not come back: GHL webhook endpoint for staging and production, auth method, the exact UTM parameter names and expected values per channel, the GTM container arrangement, the confirmation event name and fields, and whether the landing pages sit on the same domain as the booking flow. Sohib to confirm with the MedStation booking team and Rafael that the webhook is genuinely sending the full campaign payload and to get that document back.
  • Dependencies. Blocked on the booking vendor returning the spec above. Also depends on the NextGen appointment sync being reliable, which is being fixed on the Appointment Sync subitem. Building against a guessed payload shape is not worth it here, the 30 minute delay needs to be tuned against real sync timings.
  • done = a booking made through the booking app results in exactly one GHL contact carrying its UTM and campaign values alongside the synced appointment, with no duplicate contact created, verified on a live test booking.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer
